For example, if you're a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus for your Paladin spells.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the weapon mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longsword and Javelin.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the weapon mastery properties of Halberd and Flail.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

features.name: Paladin's Smite
features.description: You always have the Divine Smite spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description:
You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.

If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

features.name: Divine Sense
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the Incapacitated condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the Hallow spell.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Faithful Steed
features.description:
You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the Find Steed spell prepared.

You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Aura of Protection
features.description:
You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot Emanation [Area of Effect] that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition.

You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

If another Paladin is present, a creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time; the creature chooses which aura while in them.

features.name: Abjure Foes
features.description: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your Holy Symbol or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While Frightened in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.description: You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

features.name: Radiant Strikes
features.description: Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

features.name: Restoring Touch
features.description: When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned. You must expend 5 Hit Points from the healing pool of Lay On Hands for each of these conditions you remove; those points don't also restore Hit Points to the creature.

features.name: Aura Expansion
features.description: Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect].

features.name: Nature's Wrath
features.description: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to conjure spectral vines around nearby creatures.

features.name: Oath of the Ancients
features.description: Preserve Life and Light in the World

features.name: Oath of the Ancients Spells
features.description: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Ancients Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Aura of Warding
features.description: Ancient magic lies so heavily upon you that it forms an eldritch ward, blunting energy from beyond the Material Plane; you and your allies have Resistance to Necrotic, Psychic, and Radiant damage while in your Aura of Protection.

features.name: Undying Sentinel
features.description: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Points instead, and you regain a number of Hit Points equal to three times your Paladin level.

features.name: Elder Champion
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with primal power, granting the benefits below for 1 minute or until you end them (no action required).

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

features.name: Conquering Presence
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to exude a terrifying presence.

features.name: Guided Strike
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to strike with supernatural accuracy.

features.name: Oath of Conquest
features.description: The Oath of Conquest calls to paladins who seek glory in battle and the subjugation of their enemies.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.description: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

features.name: Tenets of Conquest
features.description: A paladin who takes this oath has the tenets of conquest seared on the upper arm.

features.name: Aura of Conquest
features.description: Starting at 7th level, you constantly emanate a menacing aura while you're not Incapacitated.

features.name: Scornful Rebuke
features.description: Starting at 15th level, those who dare to strike you are psychically punished for their audacity.

features.name: Invincible Conqueror
features.description: At 20th level, you gain the ability to harness extraordinary martial prowess.

features.name: Oath of Devotion
features.description:
Uphold the Ideals of Justice and Order

The Oath of Devotion binds Paladins to the ideals of justice and order. These Paladins meet the archetype of the knight in shining armor. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some—for better or worse—hold the rest of the world to the same standards.

Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of personal devotion. Others hold angels as their ideals and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.

These paladins share the following tenets:

Let your word be your promise.

Protect the weak and never fear to act.

Let your honorable deeds be an example.

features.name: Oath of Devotion Spells
features.description:
The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Devotion Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Oath of Devotion Spells

features.name: Sacred Weapon
features.description:
When you take the Attack action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to imbue one Melee weapon that you are holding with positive energy. For 10 minutes or until you use this feature again, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls you make with that weapon (minimum bonus of +1), and each time you hit with it, you cause it to deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage.

The weapon also emits Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light 20 feet beyond that.

You can end this effect early (no action required). This effect also ends if you aren't carrying the weapon.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.description: You and your allies have Immunity to the Charmed condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Charmed ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

features.name: Smite of Protection
features.description: Your magical smite now radiates protective energy. Whenever you cast Divine Smite, you and your allies have Cover while in your Aura of Protection. The aura has this benefit until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
features.description:
As a Bonus Action, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with holy power, granting the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

You have Advantage on any saving throw you are forced to make by a Fiend or an Undead.

Whenever an enemy starts its turn in the aura, that creature takes Radiant damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Proficiency.

The aura is filled with Bright Light that is sunlight.

features.name: Inspiring Smite
features.description: Immediately after you cast Divine Smite, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and distribute Temporary Hit Points to creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself, which can include you.

features.name: Oath of Glory
features.description: Strive for the Heights of Heroism

features.name: Oath of Glory Spells
features.description: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Glory Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Peerless Athlete
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to augment your athleticism.

features.name: Aura of Alacrity
features.description: Your Speed increases by 10 feet.

features.name: Glorious Defense
features.description: You can turn defense into a sudden strike.

features.name: Living Legend
features.description: You can empower yourself with the legends—whether true or exaggerated—of your great deeds.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

features.name: Emissary of Peace
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to augment your presence with divine power.

features.name: Oath of Redemption
features.description: The Oath of Redemption sets a paladin on a difficult path, one that requires a holy warrior to use violence only as a last resort.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.description: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

features.name: Rebuke the Violent
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to rebuke those who use violence.

features.name: Tenets of Redemption
features.description: The tenets of the Oath of Redemption hold a paladin to a high standard of peace and justice.

features.name: Aura of the Guardian
features.description: Starting at 7th level, you can shield others from harm at the cost of your own health.

features.name: Protective Spirit
features.description: Starting at 15th level, a holy presence mends your wounds in battle.

features.name: Emissary of Redemption
features.description: At 20th level, you become an avatar of peace, which gives you two benefits:

features.name: Oath of Vengeance
features.description: Punish Evildoers at Any Cost

features.name: Oath of Vengeance Spells
features.description: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Vengeance Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Vow of Enmity
features.description: When you take the Attack action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

features.name: Relentless Avenger
features.description: Your supernatural focus helps you close off a foe's retreat.

features.name: Soul of Vengeance
features.description: Immediately after a creature under the effect of your Vow of Enmity hits or misses with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to make a melee attack against that creature if it's within range.

features.name: Avenging Angel
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required).

features.name: Abjure the Extraplanar
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to castigate unworldly beings.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.description: 3rd-level Oath of the Watchers feature

features.name: Oath of the Watchers
features.description: The Oath of the Watchers binds paladins to protect mortal realms from the predations of extraplanar creatures, many of which can lay waste to mortal soldiers.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.description: 3rd-level Oath of the Watchers feature

features.name: Tenets of the Watchers
features.description: A paladin who assumes the Oath of the Watchers swears to safeguard mortal realms from otherworldly threats.

features.name: Watcher's Will
features.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to invest your presence with the warding power of your faith.

features.name: Aura of the Sentinel
features.description: 7th-level Oath of the Watchers feature

features.name: Vigilant Rebuke
features.description: 15th-level Oath of the Watchers feature

features.name: Mortal Bulwark
features.description: 20th-level Oath of the Watchers feature

features.name: Favored Enemy
features.description:
You always have the Hunter's Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a Long Rest.

The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Ranger levels, as shown in the Favored Enemy column of the Ranger Features table.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the Ranger spell list later in the class's description.

The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Ranger spells. Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Ranger Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Ranger spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Ranger Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Ranger, your list of prepared spells can include six Ranger spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Ranger feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Ranger spells for you.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots.

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells.

You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Ranger spells.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the weapon mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longbow and Shortsword.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the weapon mastery properties of Scimitar and Longsword.

features.name: Deft Explorer
features.description:
Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits.

Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in that skill.

You know two languages of your choice from the language tables in chapter 2.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Roving
features.description: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

features.name: Expertise
features.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills.

features.name: Tireless
features.description:
Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits.

As a Magic action, you can give yourself a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you finish a Short Rest, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1.

features.name: Relentless Hunter
features.description: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

features.name: Nature's Veil
features.description:
You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Precise Hunter
features.description: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

features.name: Feral Senses
features.description: Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

features.name: Foe Slayer
features.description: The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.

features.name: Beast Master
features.description: Bond with a Primal Beast

features.name: Primal Companion
features.description: You magically summon a primal beast, which draws strength from your bond with nature.

features.name: Exceptional Training
features.description: When you take a Bonus Action to command your Primal Companion beast to take an action, you can also command it to take the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action using its Bonus Action.

features.name: Bestial Fury
features.description: When you command your Primal Companion beast to take the Beast's Strike action, the beast can use it twice.

features.name: Share Spells
features.description: When you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your Primal Companion beast with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Dreadful Strikes
features.description: You can augment your weapon strikes with mind-scarring magic drawn from the murky hollows of the Feywild.

features.name: Fey Wanderer
features.description: Wield Fey Mirth and Fury

features.name: Fey Wanderer Spells
features.description: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Fey Wanderer Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Otherworldly Glamour
features.description: Whenever you make a Charisma check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

features.name: Beguiling Twist
features.description: The magic of the Feywild guards your mind.

features.name: Fey Reinforcements
features.description: You can cast Summon Fey without a Material component.

features.name: Misty Wanderer
features.description: You can cast Misty Step without expending a spell slot.

features.name: Dread Ambusher
features.description: You have mastered the art of creating fearsome ambushes, granting you the following benefits.

features.name: Gloom Stalker
features.description: Draw on Shadow Magic to Fight Your Foes

features.name: Gloom Stalker Spells
features.description: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Gloom Stalker Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Umbral Sight
features.description: You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

features.name: Iron Mind
features.description: You have honed your ability to resist mind-altering powers.

features.name: Stalker's Flurry
features.description: The Psychic damage of your Dreadful Strike becomes 2d8.

features.name: Shadowy Dodge
features.description: When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on that roll.

features.name: Detect Portal
features.description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal.

features.name: Horizon Walker
features.description: Horizon Walkers guard the world against threats that originate from other planes or that seek to ravage the mortal realm with otherworldly magic.

features.name: Horizon Walker Magic
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Horizon Walker Spells table.

features.name: Planar Warrior
features.description: At 3rd level, you learn to draw on the energy of the multiverse to augment your attacks.

features.name: Ethereal Step
features.description: At 7th level, you learn to step through the Ethereal Plane.

features.name: Distant Strike
features.description: At 11th level, you gain the ability to pass between the planes in the blink of an eye.

features.name: Spectral Defense
features.description: At 15th level, your ability to move between planes enables you to slip through the planar boundaries to lessen the harm done to you during battle.

features.name: Hunter
features.description:
Protect Nature and People from Destruction

You stalk prey in the wilds and elsewhere, using your abilities as a Hunter to protect nature and people everywhere from forces that would destroy them.

features.name: Hunter's Lore
features.description: You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey. While a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.description:
You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Your tenacity can wear down even the most resilient foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage to the target if it's missing any of its Hit Points. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, that is within the weapon's range, and that you haven't attacked this turn.

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.description:
You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Opportunity Attack have Disadvantage against you.

When a creature hits you with an attack roll, that creature has Disadvantage on all other attack rolls against you this turn.

features.name: Superior Hunter's Prey
features.description: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark, you can also deal that spell's extra damage to a different creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.

features.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
features.description: When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to give yourself Resistance to that damage and any other damage of the same type until the end of the current turn.

features.name: Hunter's Sense
features.description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to peer at a creature and magically discern how best to hurt it.

features.name: Monster Slayer
features.description: You have dedicated yourself to hunting down creatures of the night and wielders of grim magic.

features.name: Monster Slayer Magic
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Monster Slayer Spells table.

features.name: Slayer's Prey
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you can focus your ire on one foe, increasing the harm you inflict on it.

features.name: Supernatural Defense
features.description: At 7th level, you gain extra resilience against your prey's assaults on your mind and body.

features.name: Magic-User's Nemesis
features.description: At 11th level, you gain the ability to thwart someone else's magic.

features.name: Slayer's Counter
features.description: At 15th level, you gain the ability to counterattack when your prey tries to sabotage you.

features.name: Gathered Swarm
features.description: 3rd-level Swarmkeeper feature

features.name: Swarmkeeper
features.description: Feeling a deep connection to the environment around them, some rangers reach out through their magical connection to the world and bond with a swarm of nature spirits.

features.name: Swarmkeeper Magic
features.description: 3rd-level Swarmkeeper feature

features.name: Writhing Tide
features.description: 7th-level Swarmkeeper feature

features.name: Mighty Swarm
features.description: 11th-level Swarmkeeper feature

features.name: Swarming Dispersal
features.description: 15th-level Swarmkeeper feature

features.name: Expertise
features.description:
You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Sleight of Hand and Stealth are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Rogue level 6, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.description:
You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need Advantage on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition, and you don't have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.description: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in chapter 2.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the weapon mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Dagger and Shortbow.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the weapon mastery properties of Scimitar and Shortsword.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.description: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

features.name: Steady Aim
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your Speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

features.name: Cunning Strike
features.description:
You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove 1d6 from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.

If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency.

features.name: Poison (Cost: 1d6)
features.description:
You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the Poisoned target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

To use this effect, you must have a Poisoner's Kit on your person.

features.name: Trip (Cost: 1d6)
features.description: If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition.

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

features.name: Withdraw (Cost: 1d6)
features.description: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attack.

features.name: Evasion
features.description: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Reliable Talent
features.description: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

features.name: Improved Cunning Strike
features.description: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

features.name: Daze (Cost: 2d6)
features.description: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a Bonus Action.

features.name: Devious Strikes
features.description: You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

features.name: Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)
features.description: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The Unconscious target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

features.name: Obscure (Cost: 3d6)
features.description: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.description: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

features.name: Elusive
features.description: You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have Advantage against you unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.description:
You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a D20 Test, you can turn the roll into a 20.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest.

features.name: Arcane Trickster
features.description: Enhance Stealth with Arcane Spells

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.description: When you cast Mage Hand, you can cast it as a Bonus Action, and you can make the spectral hand Invisible.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description: You have learned to cast spells.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.description: If you have the Invisible condition when you cast a spell on a creature, it has Disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.description: You gain the ability to distract targets with your Mage Hand.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.description: You gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster.

features.name: Assassin
features.description: Practice the Grim Art of Death

features.name: Assassinate
features.description: You're adept at ambushing a target, granting you the following benefits.

features.name: Assassin's Tools
features.description: You gain a Disguise Kit and a Poisoner's Kit, and you have proficiency with them.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.description: You are expert at the following techniques that aid your infiltrations.

features.name: Envenom Weapons
features.description: When you use the Poison option of your Cunning Strike, the target also takes 2d6 Poison damage whenever it fails the saving throw.

features.name: Death Strike
features.description: When you hit with your Sneak Attack on the first round of a combat, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency), or the attack's damage is doubled against the target.

features.name: Ear for Deceit
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you develop a talent for picking out lies.

features.name: Eye for Detail
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot a hidden creature or object or to make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to uncover or decipher clues.

features.name: Inquisitive
features.description: As an archetypal Inquisitive, you excel at rooting out secrets and unraveling mysteries.

features.name: Insightful Fighting
features.description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to decipher an opponent's tactics and develop a counter to them.

features.name: Steady Eye
features.description: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Unerring Eye
features.description: Beginning at 13th level, your senses are almost impossible to foil.

features.name: Eye for Weakness
features.description: At 17th level, you learn to exploit a creature's weaknesses by carefully studying its tactics and movement.

features.name: Mastermind
features.description: Your focus is on people and on the influence and secrets they have.

features.name: Master of Intrigue
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the Disguise Kit, the Forgery Kit, and one Gaming Set of your choice.

features.name: Master of Tactics
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the Help action as a bonus action.

features.name: Insightful Manipulator
features.description: Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own.

features.name: Misdirection
features.description: Beginning at 13th level, you can sometimes cause another creature to suffer an attack meant for you.

features.name: Soul of Deceit
features.description: Starting at 17th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it.

features.name: Phantom
features.description: Many rogues walk a fine line between life and death, risking their own lives and taking the lives of others.

features.name: Wails from the Grave
features.description: 3rd-level Phantom feature

features.name: Whispers of the Dead
features.description: 3rd-level Phantom feature

features.name: Tokens of the Departed
features.description: 9th-level Phantom feature

features.name: Ghost Walk
features.description: 13th-level Phantom feature

features.name: Death's Friend
features.description: 17th-level Phantom feature

features.name: Scout
features.description: You are skilled in stealth and surviving far from the streets of a city, allowing you to scout ahead of your companions during expeditions.

features.name: Skirmisher
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, you are difficult to pin down during a fight.

features.name: Survivalist
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Nature and Survival skills if you don't already have it.

features.name: Superior Mobility
features.description: At 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

features.name: Ambush Master
features.description: Starting at 13th level, you excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight.

features.name: Sudden Strike
features.description: Starting at 17th level, you can strike with deadly speed.

features.name: Psi-Bolstered Knack
features.description: If you fail an ability check using a skill or tool with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning failure into success.

features.name: Psionic Power
features.description: You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself.

features.name: Psychic Blades
features.description: You can manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy.

features.name: Psychic Whispers
features.description: You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others.

features.name: Soulknife
features.description: Strike Foes with Psionic Blades

features.name: Homing Strikes
features.description: If you make an attack roll with your Psychic Blade and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the attack roll.

features.name: Psychic Teleportation
features.description: As a Bonus Action, you manifest a Psychic Blade, expend one Psionic Energy Die and roll it, and throw the blade at an unoccupied space you can see up to a number of feet away equal to 10 times the number rolled.

features.name: Soul Blades
features.description: You can now use the following powers with your Psychic Blades.

features.name: Psychic Veil
features.description: You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself.

features.name: Rend Mind
features.description: You can sweep your Psychic Blades through a creature's mind.

features.name: Fancy Footwork
features.description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to land a strike and then slip away without reprisal.

features.name: Rakish Audacity
features.description: Starting at 3rd level, your confidence propels you into battle.

features.name: Swashbuckler
features.description: You focus your training on the art of the blade, relying on speed, elegance, and charm in equal parts.

features.name: Panache
features.description: At 9th level, your charm becomes extraordinarily beguiling.

features.name: Elegant Maneuver
features.description: Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check you make during the same turn.

features.name: Master Duelist
features.description: Beginning at 17th level, your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.description:
As a Bonus Action, you can do one of the following.

Make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to pick a lock or disarm a trap with Thieves' Tools or to pick a pocket.

Take the Utilize action, or take the Magic action to use a magic item that requires that action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.description:
You've trained to get into especially hard-to-reach places, granting you these benefits.

You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

You can determine your jump distance using your Dexterity rather than your Strength.

features.name: Thief
features.description:
Hunt for Treasure as a Classic Adventurer

A mix of burglar, treasure hunter, and explorer, you are the epitome of an adventurer. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you gain abilities useful for delving into ruins and getting maximum benefit from the magic items you find there.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.description:
You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

If you have the Hide action's Invisible condition, this attack doesn't end that condition on you if you end the turn behind Cover or Cover.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.description:
You've learned how to maximize use of magic items, granting you the following benefits.

You can attune to up to four magic items at once.

Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll 1d6. On a roll of 6, you use the property without expending the charges.

You can use any Spell Scroll, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for the spell. If the spell is a cantrip or a level 1 spell, you can cast it reliably. If the scroll contains a higher-level spell, you must first succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check (DC 10 plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell from the scroll. On a failed check, the scroll disintegrates.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
features.description: You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal Initiative and your second turn at your Initiative minus 10.

features.name: Innate Sorcery
features.description:
An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1.

You have Advantage on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class's description.

You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. Light, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp, and Sorcerous Burst are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table.

The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. Burning Hands and Detect Magic are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

features.name: Font of Magic
features.description:
You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a Long Rest.

You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.

You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

As a Bonus Action, you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Sorcerer level you must be to create a slot. You can create a spell slot no higher than level 5.

Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

Creating Spell Slots

features.name: Metamagic
features.description:
Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class's description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.

features.name: Metamagic Options
features.description: The following options are available to your Metamagic feature. The options are presented in alphabetical order.

features.name: Sorcerous Restoration
features.description: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Sorcery Incarnate
features.description:
If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to activate it.

In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your Metamagic options on each spell you cast.

features.name: Arcane Apotheosis
features.description: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

features.name: Aberrant Mind
features.description: An alien influence has wrapped its tendrils around your mind, giving you psionic power.

features.name: Psionic Spells
features.description: 1st-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Telepathic Speech
features.description: 1st-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Psionic Sorcery
features.description: 6th-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Psychic Defenses
features.description: 6th-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Revelation in Flesh
features.description: 14th-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Warping Implosion
features.description: 18th-level Aberrant Mind feature

features.name: Clockwork Sorcery
features.description: Channel Cosmic Forces of Order

features.name: Clockwork Spells
features.description: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Clockwork Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Restore Balance
features.description: Your connection to the plane of absolute order allows you to equalize chaotic moments.

features.name: Bastion of Law
features.description: You can tap into the grand equation of existence to imbue a creature with a shimmering shield of order.

features.name: Trance of Order
features.description: You gain the ability to align your consciousness with the endless calculations of Mechanus.

features.name: Clockwork Cavalcade
features.description: You momentarily summon spirits of order to expunge disorder around you.

features.name: Divine Magic
features.description: Your link to the divine allows you to learn spells from the cleric class.

features.name: Divine Soul
features.description: Sometimes the spark of magic that fuels a sorcerer comes from a divine source that glimmers within the soul.

features.name: Favored by the Gods
features.description: Starting at 1st level, divine power guards your destiny.

features.name: Empowered Healing
features.description: Starting at 6th level, the divine energy coursing through you can empower healing spells.

features.name: Otherworldly Wings
features.description: Starting at 14th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest a pair of spectral wings from your back.

features.name: Unearthly Recovery
features.description: At 18th level, you gain the ability to overcome grievous injuries.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
features.description:
The magic in your body manifests physical traits of your draconic gift. Your Hit Points maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.

Parts of you are also covered by dragon-like scales. While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

features.name: Draconic Sorcery
features.description:
Breathe the Magic of Dragons

Your innate magic comes from the gift of a dragon. Perhaps an ancient dragon facing death bequeathed some of its magical power to you or your ancestor. You might have absorbed magic from a site infused with dragons' power. Or perhaps you handled a treasure taken from a dragon's hoard that was steeped in draconic power. Or you might have a dragon for an ancestor.

features.name: Draconic Spells
features.description:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Draconic Spells

features.name: Elemental Affinity
features.description:
Your draconic magic has an affinity with a damage type associated with dragons. Choose one of those types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

You have Resistance to that damage type, and when you cast a spell that deals damage of that type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

features.name: Dragon Wings
features.description:
As a Bonus Action, you can cause draconic wings to appear on your back. The wings last for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration, you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you spend 3 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

features.name: Dragon Companion
features.description:
You can cast Summon Dragon without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require Concentration. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

features.name: Eyes of the Dark
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

features.name: Shadow Magic
features.description: You are a creature of shadow, for your innate magic comes from the Shadowfell itself.

features.name: Strength of the Grave
features.description: Starting at 1st level, your existence in a twilight state between life and death makes you difficult to defeat.

features.name: Hound of Ill Omen
features.description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to call forth a howling creature of darkness to harass your foes.

features.name: Shadow Walk
features.description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to step from one shadow into another.

features.name: Umbral Form
features.description: Starting at 18th level, you can spend 6 sorcery points as a bonus action to magically transform yourself into a shadowy form.

features.name: Storm Sorcery
features.description: Your innate magic comes from the power of elemental air.

features.name: Tempestuous Magic
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to cause whirling gusts of elemental air to briefly surround you, immediately before or after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher.

features.name: Wind Speaker
features.description: The arcane magic you command is infused with elemental air.

features.name: Heart of the Storm
features.description: At 6th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

features.name: Storm Guide
features.description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to subtly control the weather around you.

features.name: Storm's Fury
features.description: Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to the attacker.

features.name: Wind Soul
features.description: At 18th level, you gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage.

features.name: Tides of Chaos
features.description: You can manipulate chaos itself to give yourself Advantage on one D20 Test before you roll the d20.

features.name: Wild Magic Sorcery
features.description: Unleash Chaotic Magic

features.name: Wild Magic Surge
features.description: Your spellcasting can unleash surges of untamed magic.

features.name: Bend Luck
features.description: You have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic.

features.name: Controlled Chaos
features.description: You gain a modicum of control over the surges of your wild magic.

features.name: Tamed Surge
features.description: Immediately after you cast a Sorcerer spell with a spell slot, you can create an effect of your choice from the Wild Magic Surge table instead of rolling on that table.

features.name: Eldritch Invocation Options
features.description: Eldritch Invocation options appear in alphabetical order.

features.name: Eldritch Invocations
features.description:
You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "Eldritch Invocation Options" section later in this class's description.

If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.

When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.

You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

features.name: Pact Magic
features.description:
Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class's description.

You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. Eldritch Blast and Prestidigitation are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.

The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest.

For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell Witch Bolt, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. Charm Person and Hex are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.

If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.

Charisma is the spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.

You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Warlock spells.

features.name: Magical Cunning
features.description: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Contact Patron
features.description:
In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the Contact Other Plane spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot to contact your patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Mystic Arcanum
features.description:
Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.

You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Warlock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 13 (level 7 spell), 15 (level 8 spell), and 17 (level 9 spell). You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.description: When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

features.name: Archfey Patron
features.description: Bargain with Whimsical Fey

features.name: Archfey Spells
features.description: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Archfey Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Steps of the Fey
features.description: Your patron grants you the ability to move between the boundaries of the planes.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.description: You can cast Misty Step as a Reaction in response to taking damage.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.description: Your patron teaches you how to guard your mind and body.

features.name: Bewitching Magic
features.description: Your patron grants you the ability to weave your magic with teleportation.

features.name: Celestial Patron
features.description: Call on the Power of the Heavens

features.name: Celestial Spells
features.description: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Celestial Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Healing Light
features.description: You gain the ability to channel celestial energy to heal wounds.

features.name: Radiant Soul
features.description: Your link to your patron allows you to serve as a conduit for radiant energy.

features.name: Celestial Resilience
features.description: You gain Temporary Hit Points whenever you use your Magical Cunning feature or finish a Short Rest or Long Rest.

features.name: Searing Vengeance
features.description: When you or an ally within 60 feet of you is about to make a Death Saving Throw, you can unleash radiant energy to save the creature.

features.name: Gift of the Sea
features.description: 1st-level Fathomless feature

features.name: Tentacle of the Deeps
features.description: 1st-level Fathomless feature

features.name: The Fathomless
features.description: You have plunged into a pact with the deeps.

features.name: Guardian Coil
features.description: 6th-level Fathomless feature

features.name: Oceanic Soul
features.description: 6th-level Fathomless feature

features.name: Grasping Tentacles
features.description: 10th-level Fathomless feature

features.name: Fathomless Plunge
features.description: 14th-level Fathomless feature

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.description: When you reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1 Temporary Hit Points). You also gain this benefit if someone else reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 Hit Points.

features.name: Fiend Patron
features.description:
Make a Deal with the Lower Planes

Your pact draws on the Lower Planes, the realms of perdition. You might forge a bargain with a demon lord such as Demogorgon or Orcus; an archdevil such as Asmodeus; or a pit fiend, balor, yugoloth, or night hag that is especially mighty. That patron's aims are evil—the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you—and your path is defined by the extent to which you strive against those aims.

features.name: Fiend Spells
features.description:
The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Fiend Spells

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.description:
You can call on your fiendish patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add 1d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), but you can use it no more than once per roll. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.description: Choose one damage type, other than Force, whenever you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest. You have Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.description:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the target disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. The target takes 8d10 Psychic damage if it isn't a Fiend, and it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn, when it returns to the space it previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

features.name: Bottled Respite
features.description: As an action, you can magically vanish and enter your vessel, which remains in the space you left.

features.name: Genie's Vessel
features.description: 1st-level Genie feature

features.name: Genie's Wrath
features.description: Once during each of your turns when you hit with an attack roll, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to your proficiency bonus.

features.name: The Genie
features.description: You have made a pact with one of the rarest kinds of genie, a noble genie.

features.name: Elemental Gift
features.description: 6th-level Genie feature

features.name: Sanctuary Vessel
features.description: 10th-level Genie feature

features.name: Limited Wish
features.description: 14th-level Genie feature

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.description: You can form a telepathic connection between your mind and the mind of another.

features.name: Great Old One Patron
features.description: Unearth Forbidden Lore of Ineffable Beings

features.name: Great Old One Spells
features.description: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Great Old One Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

features.name: Psychic Spells
features.description: When you cast a Warlock spell that deals damage, you can change its damage type to Psychic.

features.name: Clairvoyant Combatant
features.description: When you form a telepathic bond with a creature using your Awakened Mind, you can force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC.

features.name: Eldritch Hex
features.description: Your alien patron grants you a powerful curse.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.description: Your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means unless you allow it.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.description: When you cast Summon Aberration, you can modify it so that it doesn't require Concentration.

features.name: Hexblade's Curse
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to place a baleful curse on someone.

features.name: Hex Warrior
features.description: At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle.

features.name: The Hexblade
features.description: You have made your pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell—a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons carved from the stuff of shadow.

features.name: Accursed Specter
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can curse the soul of a person you slay, temporarily binding it to your service.

features.name: Armor of Hexes
features.description: At 10th level, your hex grows more powerful.

features.name: Master of Hexes
features.description: Starting at 14th level, you can spread your Hexblade's Curse from a slain creature to another creature.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.description:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Ritual Adept
features.description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class's description.

You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting Identify. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a Spell Scroll, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

features.name: Scholar
features.description: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in the chosen skill.

features.name: Memorize Spell
features.description: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.description:
You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

features.name: Signature Spells
features.description: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.description: Choose two Wizard spells from the Abjuration school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

features.name: Abjurer
features.description: Shield Companions and Banish Foes

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.description: You can weave magic around yourself for protection.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.description: When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes damage, you can take a Reaction to cause your Arcane Ward to absorb that damage.

features.name: Spell Breaker
features.description: You always have the Counterspell and Dispel Magic spells prepared.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.description: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have Resistance to the damage of spells.

features.name: Bladesinger Styles
features.description: From its inception as a martial and magical art, Bladesinging has been tied to the sword, more specifically the longsword.

features.name: Bladesinging
features.description: Bladesingers master a tradition of wizardry that incorporates swordplay and dance.

features.name: Bladesong
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can invoke a secret elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield.

features.name: Training in War and Song (Bladesinging)
features.description: When you adopt this tradition at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, and you gain proficiency with one type of one-handed melee weapon of your choice.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Song of Defense
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your bladesong is active.

features.name: Song of Victory
features.description: Starting at 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.

features.name: Divination Savant
features.description: Choose two Wizard spells from the Divination school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

features.name: Diviner
features.description: Learn the Secrets of the Multiverse

features.name: Portent
features.description: Glimpses of the future begin to press on your awareness.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.description: Casting Divination spells comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your spellcasting efforts.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.description: You can increase your powers of perception.

features.name: Greater Portent
features.description: The visions in your dreams intensify and paint a more accurate picture in your mind of what is to come.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.description:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

features.name: Evoker
features.description:
Create Explosive Elemental Effects

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.description: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.description: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.description: Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

features.name: Overchannel
features.description:
You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a Long Rest, you take 2d12 Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

Each time you use this feature again before finishing a Long Rest, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12.

features.name: Illusionist
features.description: Weave Subtle Spells of Deception

features.name: Illusion Savant
features.description: Choose two Wizard spells from the Illusion school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

features.name: Improved Illusions
features.description: You can cast Illusion spells without providing Verbal components, and if an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, the range increases by 60 feet.

features.name: Phantasmal Creatures
features.description: You always have the Summon Beast and Summon Fey spells prepared.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.description: When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between the attacker and yourself.

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.description: You have learned to weave shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semi-reality.

features.name: Awakened Spellbook
features.description: 2nd-level Order of Scribes feature

features.name: Order of Scribes
features.description: Magic of the book-that's what many folk call wizardry.

features.name: Wizardly Quill
features.description: 2nd-level Order of Scribes feature

features.name: Manifest Mind
features.description: 6th-level Order of Scribes feature

features.name: Master Scrivener
features.description: 10th-level Order of Scribes feature

features.name: One with the Word
features.description: 14th-level Order of Scribes feature

features.name: Arcane Deflection
features.description: At 2nd level, you have learned to weave your magic to fortify yourself against harm.

features.name: Tactical Wit
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, your keen ability to assess tactical situations allows you to act quickly in battle.

features.name: War Magic
features.description: A variety of arcane colleges specialize in training wizards for war.

features.name: Power Surge
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can store magical energy within yourself to later empower your damaging spells.

features.name: Durable Magic
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, the magic you channel helps ward off harm.

features.name: Deflecting Shroud
features.description: At 14th level, your Arcane Deflection becomes infused with deadly magic.
